title: Classic pivot zones — conditional wick-rejection interaction

dataset.analysis_timeframe: Conditional on parent survivors: Daily/H1 and Weekly/H4
dataset.timezone: UTC source; NY17 DST-safe pivot periods

hypotheses.market_question: Among scale-aligned pivot mappings that survive the parent study, does directionally appropriate wick rejection in the pivot core add terminal information beyond generic wick exhaustion away from pivots?
hypotheses.null: The strong-versus-weak wick terminal effect is no larger in the 0-20% pivot core than in the 30-50% outer region.
hypotheses.alternative: Strong directional wick rejection carries additional terminal information specifically inside a surviving pivot core.
hypotheses.mechanism: A wick may expose failed continuation/exhaustion at candle close; if pivot proximity adds context, the same rejection geometry should have a larger terminal association near the pivot than away from it.

method.primary_endpoint: Difference-in-differences: (core strong-wick terminal rate - core weak-wick terminal rate) - (outer strong-wick terminal rate - outer weak-wick terminal rate).
method.economic_effect_size: Percentage-point incremental wick-associated terminal probability attributable to pivot-core context beyond generic outer-region wick exhaustion.
method.event_definition: Directional wick fraction = high-side (H-max(O,C))/(H-L) or low-side (min(O,C)-L)/(H-L). Strong >=30% of candle range; weak <10%. Terminal label comes from the parent pivot-blind ATR24/0.75 detector and requires strictly later-bar confirmation.

inference.multiple_testing: Holm correction across parent-eligible mappings only

execution.same_bar_policy: wick candidate endpoint must be confirmed on a strictly later detector bar

holdout.prior_exposure: Eligibility derived only from 2015-2021 parent study; 2022-2025 untouched

provenance.notes: Eligibility was frozen from the parent gate before wick outcomes. Only D/H1 and W/H4 were tested; no failed parent mapping was admitted.
